source_text: {ΠΑΛΛ.} Τί οὖν τοῦτό γε; {ΚΥΡ.} Ὅτι, ὦ ἑταῖρε, φαίην ἂν, φορτικὸς ὁ νόμος, καὶ δύσοιστον ἄχθος· γένοιτο δ' ἂν τοῦ τοιοῦδε μήνυσις ἐναργὴς, τὸ μὴ εἰς ὤμους φέρεσθαι τὰ περισσὰ, διά τοι τὸ ἀσθενεῖν τοὺς ὑπεζευγμένους. Τοιγάρτοι καὶ ἔφασκον οἱ θεσπέσιοι μαθηταὶ, τοῖς μετὰ τὴν πίστιν ἐπὶ νομικὴν ἰοῦσι λατρείαν· «Καὶ νῦν τί πειράζετε τὸν Θεὸν, ἐπιθεῖναι ζυγὸν ἐπὶ τὸν τράχηλον τῶν μαθητῶν, ὃν οὔτε ὑμεῖς, οὔτε οἱ πατέρες ὑμῶν ἴσχυσαν βαστάσαι;» Κααθῖται δὲ, τὰ δι' ὧν ὁ Χριστὸς σημαίνεται, τοῖς σφῶν αὐτ
pass_a_gloss: §8 dual gloss: ζυγὸν / yoke; φορτίον / load … Pass A ≠ Pass B. Theme: Law a hard yoke; Christ’s light burden; first/last peoples; Korah begi
pass_b_english: Palladius: What then is this at least?

Cyril: That, O companion, I would say, burdensome is the law, and a hard-to-bear load; and a clear indication of such would become, the leftovers not being carried unto shoulders, through at least the yoked being weak. Therefore also the all-divine disciples were saying to those going after the faith unto legal worship: ‘And now why do you test God, to set a yoke upon the neck of the disciples, which neither you nor your fathers were strong to bear?’ And Kohathites, having set upon their own shoulders the things through which Christ is signaled, make a light and well-portable load. So then is this not clearly what Christ himself said: ‘My yoke is kind, and my load light’?

Cyril: And I would still add to the things said also this. For it would not be unhelpful unto full-assurance; for in the first enrollment of the Levites, those from Gershon had been ranked in beginnings, then middle Kohath, and last Merari (and these Levitical peoples); and in the second, the from twenty and five years, Kohath has been set toward of the others, and has been named first. And last after him, Gershon and Merari, having as liturgy the leftovers of the tent. And each of these two peoples have only up to two patriaries, and the one goes forward even until four. So then do you understand the riddle?

Cyril: For Israel has been called in firsts; and with the herd of the nations having run-in between, he has been ranked after this; and the lasts have become firsts, according to the Savior’s voice, and the firsts lasts.
Cyril: And that short in number of the Jews is the people, with the unmeasured multitude from nations overlying by much, is clear.

Cyril: Therefore God says toward hierophant Moses: ‘And now leave me, and having been angered I will consume-out this synagogue, and I will make you unto a great nation, and much more than this.’ So then with such liturgies the whole Levitical band has been honored; and a bound for them of the sacred-work to be yoked to the outstanding, and to do under hand the of Aaron. And at least to think over this and to seek the better of the things distributed to him and defined by God, was being shown through the trial itself as procurer of penalty and destruction.
